definition: The institutional Church whose binding teaching office is exercised by the Roman Pontiff and the bishops collectively in communion with him, through council or ordinary-universal teaching, rather than any assertion by a member or office-holder. This is the subject of the CDF classification, used for the skeleton’s named Catholic society.
note: The source distinction is Doctrinal Commentary nn. 4 and 9. The classification is consulted as evidence of the Church’s proposal status; publication by the CDF is not thereby called a new solemn definition. This does not identify the modern society with the Church founded by Christ or establish divine authority; those remain separate skeleton premises.
